title: Proof
body_md: Existence, uniqueness and upper moment bounds follow from Wiener chaos expansions and heat kernel estimates, extending the approach of~\cite{BCHOTW24}. For H\"older continuity, we use the weak Bakry--\'Emery estimates developed in~\cite{Besov3}. To prove existence of the Lyapunov exponents, we first construct the fundamental solution and its stochastic flow, extending the framework of Alberts, Khanin and Quastel~\cite{AlbertsKhaninQuastel2014}. We then adapt the moment comparisons of Berger, Chong and Lacoin~\cite[Lemma~5.1 and proof of Proposition~2.8]{BergerChongLacoin2023}.The argument applies to every real $p\ge1$ without spatial translation invariance. Finally, the Gaussian exponential test of~\cite[Proposition~3.20]{ChenDeyaOuyangTindel2021}, combined with confinement of the diffusion to a ball, gives lower bounds for every real $p>1$.

title: Example
body_md: Assumption~\ref{hyp:dirichlet-form} is satisfied by $\mathbb{R}^d$ with Lebesgue measure and the standard Dirichlet form, Carnot groups of homogeneous dimension $Q$, and complete $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature and maximal volume growth. In these cases $d_w=2$ and $d_h=d,Q,d$, respectively. It also holds on unbounded nested fractals~\cite{Barlow1998,Kigami2001}, including the infinite Sierpi\'nski gasket~\cite{BarlowPerkins1988}, for which $d_h=\log3/\log2$ and $d_w=\log5/\log2$, and on unbounded generalized Sierpi\'nski carpets~\cite{BarlowBass1999}. In the last two families $d_w>2$, and both the strictly recurrent regime $d_h<d_w$ and the regime $d_h\ge d_w$ occur.

label: lem:tail-exit-UB
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Set $\lambda=(R^{d_w}/s)^{1/(d_w-1)}\ge1$ and $\gamma=d_w/(d_w-1)$. Decomposing $\{d(\cdot,z)\ge R\}$ into the annuli $A_n=B(z,2^{n+1}R)\setminus B(z,2^nR)$, $n\ge0$, and using the upper bound in~\eqref{eq:subGauss} together with the Ahlfors regularity, we get
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{P}_z\bigl(d(B_s,z)\ge R\bigr)&\le\sum_{n\ge0}Cs^{-d_h/d_w}e^{-c2^{n\gamma}\lambda}\mu\bigl(B(z,2^{n+1}R)\bigr)
\\
&\le C\Bigl(\frac{R^{d_w}}{s}\Bigr)^{d_h/d_w}\sum_{n\ge0}2^{nd_h}e^{-c2^{n}\lambda}\,.
\end{align*}
For $\lambda\ge1$, the series is bounded by $Ce^{-c\lambda}$. Since $(R^{d_w}/s)^{d_h/d_w}=\lambda^{d_h(d_w-1)/d_w}$, the polynomial factor can be absorbed by decreasing $c$. This proves~\eqref{eq:oneParticleTail}.

label: lem:sobolev-IP
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:Kernel-2alpha-correspondence} and Tonelli's theorem,
\begin{equation*}
\int_X\Bigl(\int_XG_\gamma(x,y)|f(y)|\,d\mu(y)\Bigr)^2d\mu(x)=\int_X\int_X|f(y)||f(z)|G_{2\gamma}(y,z)\,d\mu(y)d\mu(z)<\infty\,,
\end{equation*}
which shows that $G_\gamma|f|\in L^2$; in particular $G_\gamma|f|<\infty$ a.e., so $G_\gamma f$ is a.e.\ absolutely convergent and $|G_\gamma f|\le G_\gamma|f|$. The same holds for $g$, and by Cauchy--Schwarz the function $(x,y,z)\mapsto f(y)g(z)G_\gamma(x,y)G_\gamma(x,z)$ is integrable on $X^3$. Fubini's theorem and Lemma~\ref{lem:Kernel-2alpha-correspondence} then give~\eqref{eq:sobolev-IP}, and taking $f=g$ shows the positive semidefiniteness.  If $f\in L^1\cap L^\infty$, then estimate~\eqref{eq:G-integrable},
which was proved for every exponent in $(0,d_h/d_w)$, applies
with $2\gamma$ in place of $\gamma$, since $2\gamma<d_h/d_w$. Thus, $\sup_y\int_X|f(x)|G_{2\gamma}(x,y)\,d\mu(x)<\infty$, so that $\iint|f(x)||f(y)|G_{2\gamma}(x,y)\le C\|f\|_{L^1}<\infty$. Finally, \eqref{eq:sobolev-IP-S} follows from~\eqref{eq:sobolev-IP} and Lemma~\ref{lem:fractional-laplacian-kernel-is-a-kernel}.

title: Remark
body_md: For $\alpha>0$, in the Euclidean case $d_w=2$, $\kappa=1$, the exponents of Theorem~\ref{thm:Holder} are $(2+4\alpha-d_h)/4$ in time and $(2+4\alpha-d_h)/2$ in space for the Riesz covariance $|x-y|^{4\alpha-d_h}$, $0<d_h-4\alpha<2$. These coincide with the exponents in~\cite[Theorem~1.8]{ChenHuang2019} for the equation driven by noise that is white in time and has Riesz spatial covariance. At $\alpha=0$, necessarily $d_h<d_w$, the corresponding exponents are $(d_w-d_h)/(2d_w)$ in time and $\min\{\kappa,(d_w-d_h)/2\}$ in space; for $X=\mathbb{R}$ these are $1/4$ and $1/2$. For compact p.c.f.\ fractals, space-time regularity was studied for the additive equation in~\cite{HamblyYang2018} and for nonlinear equations, including PAM, in~\cite{HamblyYang2026}. On standard nested fractals their white-noise exponents, expressed in the metric $d$, agree with $(d_w-d_h)/(2d_w)$ in time and $(d_w-d_h)/2$ in space. In the present theorem the space exponent is also limited by exponent $\kappa$.

label: rem:compact-moment-comparison
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:compact-moment-comparison}
For $\alpha>0$ and integer $p\ge2$, Theorem~\ref{thm:moment-LB} is the analogue of~\cite[Theorem~3.16]{BCHOTW24} in the present setting.  At $\alpha=0$, the second-moment lower bound can also be obtained by the renewal argument of~\cite[Section~3.6.2]{BCHOTW24}. For the PAM on compact p.c.f.\ fractals, Hambly and Yang~\cite{HamblyYang2026} prove weak intermittency and predict moment-order growth with exponent $2+D$, where $D$ is the Hausdorff dimension in the resistance metric. On standard nested fractals, $D=d_h/(d_w-d_h)$, so this exponent agrees with $1+d_w/(d_w-d_h)$ in our whole-space bounds.
